### Archer to Shape Physical AI Future of Aerospace and Defense with Acquisition of Boeing's Wisk Aero, Insitu and SkyGrid Subsidiaries; Boeing to Invest in Archer and Collaborate

August 10, 2026

* Transaction creates an end-to-end physical AI platform for aerospace and defense.
* Adds a profitable defense business generating over $200M in annual revenue ¹ , with operations across 35 countries, to Archer's portfolio.
* Combines Wisk, SkyGrid and Insitu's pioneering autonomy and airspace intelligence software with Archer's leading purpose-built AI foundation model for aerospace and defense, ZEE.
* Boeing to take stake and become a strategic partner to Archer; establishes ongoing Archer and Boeing collaboration and technology sharing arrangement.

ARLINGTON, Va. and SILICON VALLEY, Calif. , Aug. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Boeing Company (NYSE: BA) and Archer Aviation Inc.
(NYSE: ACHR) today announced the companies have signed definitive agreements in which Archer will acquire Boeing's Wisk Aero, SkyGrid and Insitu subsidiaries. The deal will combine complementary capabilities developed over decades in autonomy, electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft, and unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) – creating a groundbreaking end-to-end physical AI platform for aerospace and defense.

Wisk, SkyGrid and Insitu have pioneered and incubated core autonomous flight technologies for the future that, in combination with Archer's air taxi, UAS and AI technologies, will bring new and innovative solutions to the market. These companies, with nearly two million combined flight hours, are expected to bring a deep autonomy foundation to Archer's ZEE artificial intelligence platform. This positions Archer to deliver an end-to-end physical AI platform across commercial aerospace, defense and air traffic management that can lead the next generation of aviation.

...

"It allows Wisk, SkyGrid and Insitu to accelerate capability development and time to market while ensuring Boeing capitalizes on its investments in these technologies over the past two decades through continued development in our core businesses. Having worked with the incredible teams in these companies firsthand, it's clear this transaction will create an industry leader in the advanced aviation market. We look forward to collaborating with Archer to drive continued innovation in aerospace, defense and autonomy."

About the companies:

* [Wisk](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4748626-1&h=3611892879&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwisk.aero%2F&a=Wisk) is the only company that has designed, built and flown six generations of eVTOL aircraft, amassing 1,700+ flight tests.

...

Its product portfolio spans high-performance, cost-effective, resilient, VTOL-capable UAS and AI-enabled software solutions. Insitu's technologies have helped the armed forces of 35 nations make quicker, more informed decisions to bring warfighters home safely. With offices in the US, Australia, the UK, and the UAE, Insitu has manufactured and fielded more than 3,500 UAS and provides operations and support networks in every hemisphere of the globe.

Additional details of the transaction are available in Archer's Form 8-K filed today with the Securities and Exchange Commission. The transaction remains subject to certain agreed-upon closing conditions, including expiration or termination of the waiting period under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act and is expected to close by the end of 2026. * 

The transaction encompasses three distinct companies which together account for nearly two million flight hours: Wisk Aero, SkyGrid, and Insitu. The deal is expected to close by the end of 2026 and remains subject to regulatory approvals. Financial details, including the purchase price and the extent of Boeing’s future stake in Archer, have not been disclosed.

As reported by _Aerotelegraph_ , Archer’s core eVTOL business is central to the deal – particularly where Wisk Aero is concerned.
Wisk Aero has spent 16 years developing autonomous eVTOLs and has completed over 1,700 test flights, according to its records. While Archer’s own eVTOL, Midnight, will initially operate with a pilot, the acquisition of Wisk lays the technology groundwork for future autonomous operations to the company. SkyGrid, meanwhile, provides software for automated air traffic management, supporting the integration of autonomous and unmanned aerial vehicles into airspace.

Archer and Wisk share a history: [In 2021,](https://www.electrive.net/2021/04/16/wisk-aero-verklagt-archer-aviation/) Wisk sued its competitor for alleged theft of trade secrets ( _link in German_ ) [.](https://www.electrive.net/2021/04/16/wisk-aero-verklagt-archer-aviation/) The dispute was settled in 2023, after which Boeing invested in Archer, and the two companies agreed to collaborate on autonomy technologies. Now, Wisk is fully transitioning under Archer’s umbrella.

## Archer expands business beyond eVTOLs
The acquisition of Insitu adds another dimension to the transaction. The company specialises in unmanned aerial systems, particularly for reconnaissance and surveillance missions. What’s more, it has reportedly delivered over 3,500 systems and is profitable, with annual revenues exceeding $200 million US dollars. This aligns with Archer’s growing focus on defence: since late 2024, the company has collaborated with Anduril on a hybrid VTOL aircraft for military applications and introduced Thunder, an autonomous VTOL aircraft, in July 2026. In parallel, Archer is advancing the commercial use of electric aircraft: in July, the company announced the ACES charging infrastructure consortium alongside BETA Technologies and Macquarie Capital. The consortium aims to equip more than [250 sites across the USA by 2030](https://www.electrive.com/2026/07/21/archer-and-beta-plan-250-charging-sites-for-electric-aircraft/) .
This significantly broadens Archer’s strategy: Midnight remains its flagship electric aircraft, while Wisk and SkyGrid provide autonomy and air traffic management solutions. Insitu contributes an established drone business, and ACES delivers the charging infrastructure. However, the speed at which these elements can be integrated into commercial eVTOL operations still depends on progress in certification and market ramp-up.

Boeing is not fully exiting the picture: a parallel technology partnership ensures the corporation retains access to Wisk’s technologies, and Boeing will also hold a future stake in Archer. Archer describes the combination of autonomy, eVTOLs, drones, and software as the foundation of a ‘Physical AI’ platform for aviation and defence. With this deal, Archer is evolving from a manufacturer primarily focused on electric air taxis into a more diversified aviation company.

The aircraft giant will acquire nearly 20% of Archer’s Class A shares and make a future stock investment in the company.

### Dive Brief:

* Boeing is selling three of its subsidiaries to Archer Aviation in exchange for a minority stake in the electric aircraft startup , [according to a securities filing](https://d18rn0p25nwr6d.cloudfront.
net/CIK-0001824502/0ffc30eb-a744-4999-833b-b66524aa61c1.pdf=43) Monday.
* Archer has agreed to acquire Wisk Aero, a maker of electric vertical take-off and landing aircraft; drone company Insitu; and air traffic software firm Skygrid. Boeing’s stake in Archer will amount to 19.75% of Class A shares with options to buy more shares over the next four years, according to the filing.
* Boeing has also agreed to invest up to $55 million in stock in Archer’s next funding round, [any time before March 31, 2027](https://d18rn0p25nwr6d.cloudfront.net/CIK-0001824502/81397d5a-5a20-4830-9e27-811746cd976e.pdf=4) . The sale is expected to close by the end of 2026.

### Dive Insight:

The pending sale allows Boeing to prioritize its commercial, defense and global services, focusing on safety and quality of its plane manufacturing processes.

In 2025, the plane titan sold a portion of its digital aviation software business unit to private equity software firm [Thoma Bravo for $10.
55 billion](https://www.manufacturingdive.com/news/boeing-selling-portion-of-digital-aviation-solutions-assets-thoma-brava/745968/) . The company also [reacquired fuselage supplier Spirit Aerosystems](https://www.manufacturingdive.com/news/boeing-completes-83b-spirit-aerosystems-acquisition/807298/) for $8.4 billion, while also selling some of its assets to rival Airbus in an effort to comply with global government requirements.

In addition to Boeing’s stake in Archer, the agreement also involves the two companies collaborating on improving and developing new products, Archer CEO and Chairman Adam Goldstein said during a [second quarter earnings call Monday](https://seekingalpha.com/article/4934329-archer-aviation-inc-achr-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript) .

Once the deal closes, Archer will own the Wisk intellectual property.

Furthermore, Archer agreed to make Wisk the exclusive autonomy technology provider for new aircraft models.

While Archer’s main focus is still electric air taxis, the company has been diversifying its aerospace portfolio to include applications in the defense sector.

In July, Archer and defense startup Anduril unveiled two autonomous aircraft variants that they’ve been developing at the [Farnborough International Airshow](https://www.manufacturingdive.com/news/electra-beehive-ohio-gkn-rtx-doncasters-farnborough-air-show-2026/826082/) in England, [Halo](https://www.archer.com/halo) and [Thunder](https://www.anduril.com/thunder) .

Halo is an autonomous VTOL intended for commercial and defense use. For commercial clients, it’s expected to be used primarily for cargo and rescue operations, according to the Q2 securities filing.

Thunder is a Group 5 autonomous attack drone.
